Annual calibration and preventative maintenance of Comark transmitters will be conducted by
TGA Industries Limited / Setra® Systems, an approved service provider.
RF512 – Onsite Calibration (Temperature Monitoring)· Comark Transmitters RF512 will be temporarily removed from their installed location for the same day on-site calibration.
· During the calibration period of each RF512 unit will be replaced with a Tinytag Ultra 2 temperature data logger to ensure continuous temperature monitoring of critical location.
· On completion of calibration, the RF512 transmitters will be reinstalled in their original locations.
· Any temperature excursions recorded on the Tinytag Ultra 2 devices during the calibration period
will be assessed and investigated in accordance with ES.SOP.015 – Deviation Management.
RF512 – Offsite Calibration (Temperature Monitoring)
· Comark Transmitters RF513 will be removed from their respective locations and sent offsite for
calibration.
· During the offsite calibration period, loan equipment will be supplied by Setra® (equivalent
calibrated Comark RF513 transmitters capable of monitoring temperature & humidity) will be installed to maintain uninterrupted environmental monitoring.
· The loan equipment will remain in use until the original RF513 transmitters are calibrated, returned and reinstalled.
· Any temperature or humidity excursions recorded during this period will be investigated in accordance with procedure ES.SOP.015 – Deviation Management.
This change is temporary and limited to the duration of the annual calibration activities.

Update Trihexyphenidyl hydrochloride Suspensions BMR by replacing Trihexyphenidyl 5mg tablets with Trihexyphenidyl Hydrochloride powder.

Trihexyphenidyl Hydrochloride powder as an API form was not available in the required amount direct from Eaststone approved suppliers. Due to this reason, and as an alternative, Trihexyphenidyl Hydrochloride 5mg Tablets have been used in bespoke (unlicensed) extemporaneous liquid formulations to fulfil the supply of these products. 

Since Trihexyphenidyl Hydrochloride API powder is now available in required quantity and pack size from Eaststone’s current approved suppliers, this has been ordered by procurement department. 

Based on the above, R&D department will review and update the formulations, if possible, for the current Trihexyphenidyl Hydrochloride Oral Suspension products.

Purchase, installation, qualification, and routine GMP use of a pharmaceutical Oscillating Granulator for size reduction and uniform sizing of wet and/or dry granules used in solid oral dosage form manufacturing.

The equipment will be installed in the designated GMP manufacturing area and operated in accordance with an approved User Requirement Specification (URS). Associated validation activities, SOP generation, and personnel training will be completed prior to routine use.
The Oscillating Granulator is required to:
•	Achieve consistent and controlled granule size distribution
•	Improve process efficiency and reproducibility
•	Support downstream processing (compression / encapsulation)
•	Replace or supplement existing granulation capability (if applicable)
•	Ensure GMP-compliant equipment design with improved cleanability and safety
The equipment will be qualified and validated before use; therefore, no adverse impact on product quality is anticipated.

The proposed change entails repackaging the Midazolam API Powder, originally supplied by APS in a large plastic drum, into a smaller suitable GMP- compliant container.

The originally supplied container is not fully suitable for routine weighing or dispensing operations due to its size and weight. Typically, only small quantities of Midazolam Powder are required to fulfil individual orders and weighing very small quantities from the supplied container on the three-point scale is not operationally feasible. 
To minimise disruptions to manufacturing operations and ensure continued compliance with internal handling and weighing processes, the API must be repackaged into a smaller container that is compatible with existing weighing balances.
The proposed change will:
•	Enable efficient and safe material handling and weighing procedures.
•	Support continued compliance with GMP requirements during production.
•	Ensure complete and accurate reconciliation for dispensing controlled drugs 
•	Prevent operational inefficiencies, delays, or deviations that could affect product quality or workflow.

The proposed change presents minimal risk as the repackaging will involve only tertiary packaging, which does not come into direct contact with the product, ensuring there is no impact on product quality or safety. Additionally, the new container will be sourced from an approved supplier and the transfer will be conducted under controlled GMP conditions. 
Prior to use, the new container will undergo thorough cleaning to ensure adherence to hygiene and compliance standards. The change is not expected to adversely affect supply chain operations, logistics, or sales and it does not introduce any significant financial impact.
